::: {.lund-lead}
How can AI help with the mathematics students are **actually studying**?
:::

## The frame {#frame .lund-part data-part="0"}

::: {.lund-big}
For the next ten years, the social contract still holds.
:::

- Universities **certify**: a degree says the candidate passed the exams.
- Knowledge is **chunked**: a programme into courses, a course into topics.
- AI or not, the lower-level chunks will most likely survive.

::: {.lund-nest}
::: {.lund-box}
**Study programme**

::: {.lund-box}
**Course**

::: {.lund-box}
**Topic**

[Definition]{.lund-chip} [Notation]{.lund-chip} [Example]{.lund-chip} [Method]{.lund-chip} [Exercise]{.lund-chip}
:::
:::
:::
:::

::: {.lund-cols}
::: {.lund-card .lund-inside}
### Inside the course

Our definitions, our notation, our examples, our methods, what is assessed.
:::

::: {.lund-card .lund-outside}
### Outside the course

Everything else: other books, other conventions, other levels.
:::
:::

## Retrieval-Augmented Generation {#rag .lund-part data-part="2"}

::: {.lund-big}
One way to define the course for a model: let it read the course.
:::

::::: {.lund-steps .lund-steps-compact}
::: {.lund-step}
**Retrieve**\
find the pages of the course that fit the question
:::
::: {.lund-step}
**Augment**\
hand those pages to the model with the question
:::
::: {.lund-step}
**Generate**\
the model answers from them, and says which pages
:::
:::::

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 9
%%{init: {"themeVariables": {"fontSize": "18px"}}}%%
flowchart LR
  S([Student asks]) --> L["Librarian<br/>finds the right pages"]
  L --> M["Language model<br/>writes the answer"]
  M --> A([Answer + the pages it used])
  C[(The course,<br/>in short passages)] --- L
  classDef course fill:#fff8ec,stroke:#e8a33d
  classDef model fill:#eaf6ee,stroke:#2e8b57
  classDef student fill:#eef5fd,stroke:#2780e3
  class C,L course
  class M model
  class S,A student
```

### What lives where

::: {.lund-where}
::: {.lund-place .is-github}
**The course pages**\
where the teacher writes them: GitHub
:::
::: {.lund-place .is-server}
**The librarian and the passages**\
a small private server; updated whenever the course changes
:::
::: {.lund-place .is-cluster}
**The language model**\
Idun, NTNU's large computing cluster; nothing leaves NTNU
:::
::: {.lund-place .is-browser}
**The student**\
only a web browser
:::
:::

::: {.lund-question}
**Inside first**: the answer comes from the course pages, and names them.
**Outside if needed**: anything else comes after, clearly labelled.
:::

[Open the course assistant]({{< meta rag-url >}}){.btn .btn-primary .btn-lg .lund-cta}

## One source, two uses {#source .lund-part data-part="3"}

::: {.lund-big}
The teacher writes the course once. Students read it; the assistant reads it too.
:::

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 8
flowchart LR
  T([Teacher]) --> Q["Course pages in Quarto<br/>text · mathematics · code"]
  Q --> G[(GitHub repository)]
  G --> W([Website<br/>students see])
  G --> I([Course index<br/>the assistant reads])
```

- Change the notes, and both the website and the assistant follow.
- No separate "AI version" of the course.

## The point {#point .lund-part}

::: {.lund-takeaways}
- **The course** sets the frame: what is inside, what is outside.
- **Checks** are explicit and reproducible.
- **AI** works inside that frame, and says when it steps out.
:::
